column1: # Concepts we propose adding to KinDiv, with Hmong as the motivating evidence.
# These are in KinDiv's own `wn/extra-concepts.tsv` format, so they can be pasted
# straight in. The `relations` rows follow, in `wn/extra-relations.tsv` format.
# Why these four. Hmong `nus`, `muam`, `tij laug` and `kwv` name the child of a
# father's sibling *regardless of whether that sibling is a brother or a sister*,
# while distinguishing the sex of the speaker and, for the last two, relative age.
# Upstream KinDiv uses `Fa;Sb;So` and `Fa;Sb;Da` in `relations` and `gaps` but never
# listed them in `concepts` (an omission, not a deletion: `concepts` has never had
# them). It has no speaker-sex or age-marked variants of them at all. So the
# structure is there and the labels are not, and Hmong is evidence that a language
# lexicalises exactly these.
# Two of the six are the base concepts KinDiv uses without declaring; the other
# four are what Hmong actually needs.
# STATUS (2026-09-28): all six are in fcbond/KinDiv. `Fa;Sb;So` and `Fa;Sb;Da` were
# added to `concepts` itself; the four speaker-sex concepts and their relations are
# in `wn/extra-concepts.tsv` and `wn/extra-relations.tsv`, marked "pending
# confirmation". The Hmong words, with those of kinship-kindiv.tsv, are in
# `wn/attested-words.tsv`. The relations also link each concept to its speaker-sex
# cousin concept (e.g. o;Fa;Sb;So under o;Pa;Sb;So, "male cousin (female speaking)").
# CHECK: Nathan -- confirm that Hmong `nus`, `muam`, `tij laug` and `kwv` really are
# indifferent to whether the father's sibling is a brother or a sister. If they are
# not, these collapse to the existing Fa;Br;* and Fa;Ss;* concepts and no proposal
# is needed.
# Why we doubt it. Hmong clans are patrilineal and exogamous, so a father's
# brother's children belong to ego's clan, but a father's sister's children
# belong to her husband's. The ethnographic expectation is that they are
# *npawg*, like the mother's side, and that `nus`/`muam`/`tij laug`/`kwv` extend
# only to the father's BROTHER's children (Fa;Br;So, Fa;Br;Da). This is an
# expectation, not something checked against White (2021). If it holds:
#   - `nus` and `muam` map to the existing o;Fa;Br;So and x;Fa;Br;Da; `tij laug`
#     and `kwv` would need x;El;Fa;Br;So and x;Yn;Fa;Br;So, which are still new
#     (KinDiv has El;Fa;Br;So and x;Fa;Br;So, but none marks both relative age and
#     speaker sex);
#   - `npawg` and `muam npaws` in kinship-kindiv.tsv are broader than Mo;Sb;So and
#     Mo;Sb;Da (they would also cover Fa;Ss;So and Fa;Ss;Da), so those rows should
#     become `narrower`, not `exact`.
